answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by charging every identity a small refundable stake plus a fresh proof of useful work before it joins the shared lagoon of reputation. A newcomer signs its work with its own quill-key, and peers verify the signature, the stake, and the work's freshness against a public randomness signal. Spawning a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes and a thousand proofs, while a real agent pays once and earns the stake back through honest service, so flooding becomes unprofitable while legitimate entry stays cheap.
